analysis.conclusion: New direct grid-template-columns follows the original equal-specificity .workbench-grid rule in the same stylesheet. Inline style supplies custom properties only, so it cannot override the new direct property. Later explicit grid-column/grid-row assignments preserve center in track 3 and do not redefine tracks. Repository CSS search found no other workbench-grid/pane definitions.

At CSS widths <=819 the side and divider tracks are zero and center takes available width even if React width retains a desktop value. At 820, 900, 1279, 1280 and wider the new rule does not apply; existing Shell >=820 navigation and >=1280 Agent decisions remain unchanged. No saved panel widths or collapse states are overwritten.

The selector is a CSS viewport media query, with no device width or devicePixelRatio gate. Existing real-zoom test selects Chrome 200%, measures CSS width halving, checks nav hidden and no page overflow. That existing test has been inspected only, not rerun for this source by this reviewer.

Only workbench-grid tracks change; drawer dialogs are outside that grid. Existing Shell callback updates width and closes any stale drawer; in narrow state the toolbar opens navigation/Agent native modal dialogs. Controls preserves Escape/close/focus return. No permanent display:none or removal rule was added for dialog content.

New test imports and submits a real assessment through a private RestartRuntime, waits for real needs_review, holds delivery of actual resize listeners while browser layout resizes to 390, then asserts center width and the original paragraph viewport property before callbacks release. Release and runtime/browser cleanup are in finally. It does not stub layout, grades or server responses.
